scope: Profile setup/startup/repair, provider config and .env writes use bounded nofollow/identity-checked private storage.
Existing Windows ACLs verify-only; new empty objects restricted before content. POSIX existing modes unchanged, published config/.env0600.
First runtime installation admits a new owned home before bootstrap descendants, after validation. Existing unsafe homes refuse before installer work.
Shipped skills copied as verified bounded private files without replacing locally maintained skills.
Unused Windows legacy recursive migration fails before source/destination mutation; POSIX behavior retained.
Synchronous ACL export reuses unchanged existing PowerShell policy and sanitized error taxonomy.
Profile IDs, provider routing, upstream Hermes, native memory helpers and public Windows memory holds were not changed by this wave.
limits: No native Windows execution: ACL effects, NTFS sharing/publication, genuine Windows setup and native memory admission remain unverified.
Six actual-Windows ACL tests were skipped on macOS; simulated ACL tests are not native proof.
Existing broad Hermes test fixtures may require explicit private ACL preparation before a genuine Windows CI run.
Installed-profile startup performs eight to nine sequential verify-only PowerShell checks, each with a 15-second timeout; real Windows startup latency is unmeasured.
Config and .env are separate whole-file operations; this does not create a multi-file transaction or automatic rollback after uncertain publication.

Profile provisioning uses Node filesystem identity checks and path publication, not the unadmitted native journal handle/locking protocol; no adversarial same-user writer or physical power-loss guarantee is claimed.
No new Grok review was launched; separate CLI timeout diagnosis remains with another agent.
